messages:
alex: Quick check — I opened a tiny TF change to add an `owner` label to model-config ConfigMaps so we can gate rollouts in CI. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482

morgan: Nice. Is this just a metadata label or will the controller read it for rollouts?

alex: Metadata only initially. Plan is CI will reject applies when owner is empty, and later the rollout controller will refuse automated rollforward if owner != oncall team. small safety step.
sanjay: pinged infra-sre about naming convention. We should use `team/owner` vs `owner`? terraform code currently writes `redwood.owner` in other places.

kate: prefer `team/owner` so it's consistent with k8s recommended label prefixes. Also avoids collisions with third-party tools.
luis: I can update the TF to write `team/owner` and add a unit test in terratest. Good to automate.
alex: thanks — I already added a comment in the PR asking for that. Also added a `configmap_checksum` annotation we can increment when we want a manual rollout: `redwood/configmap-version: vYYYYMMDD-HHMM`
morgan: can you paste the snippet you added?
alex: sure:

```hcl
resource "kubernetes_config_map" "model_config" {
  metadata {
    name = "model-config-${var.model_name}"
    labels = {
      "team/owner" = var.owner
      "redwood/managed-by" = "model-config-operator"
    }
    annotations = {
      "redwood/configmap-version" = var.configmap_version
    }
  }
  data = local.data_map
}
```

sanjay: thanks. Two quick Qs: 1) how is `var.owner` populated for existing stacks? 2) if owner is missing, will CI block the whole org apply or just the resource?
alex: 1) I'm adding a migration plan to populate from `team` tag in TF state for known stacks, with an interactive fallback for ambiguous ones. 2) CI will fail the apply job for that workspace only — we don't want to nuke everything.

kate: for the migration, can we have a dry-run that lists which workspaces would be affected? That helps SRE to reach out.
luis: easy — terraform plan + a grep for `team/owner` absent in rendered manifest. I can add that script to the PR checks.
alex: great. Also adding a prettier error message in CI:

```
ERROR: model-config missing required label `team/owner`.
Please set `var.owner` in the workspace tfvars or run `./scripts/set-owner.sh`.
```

morgan: one more: secrets wiring — some services infer owner from secret annotations. Do we need to sync secret labels too?

sanjay: yes, the secret syncer expects `redwood/owner` on secrets. We should add a small helm hook that copies `team/owner` from configmap -> secret metadata on deploy. Otherwise the syncer will skip them.
alex: noted — adding a follow-up ticket to add the hook and update the operator. #TICKET-314

deploy-bot: deploy-check for infra/pr/482 completed — plan shows 3 additions, 0 deletions. No diffs for production workspaces in the org.

kate: OK lets do this in two phases: (1) land TF change + CI check + dry-run migration listing, (2) add secret sync hook and operator change. If anyone is blocked by owner missing after migration, tag @sre-oncall.
luis: I'll pick up the CI script and terratest today, aim for EOD PR update.

morgan: I'll review when ready, try to catch the migration edges. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

alex: thanks! tagging owners for follow-ups: @luis @sanjay @kate.
